    AI Overview
    The Outer Banks (OBX) is a 100-mile stretch of barrier islands off the North Carolina coast, renowned as a top vacation destination for its beaches, history, and coastal charm. Key attractions include the Cape Hatteras National Seashore, Wright Brothers National Memorial, and Jockey’s Ridge. Summers are popular, but spring and fall offer milder weather. 
    This video shows some of the highlights of a trip to the Outer Banks:
    58s
    Puttering around the World
    YouTube• Apr 7, 2026
    Top Things to Do 
    • Beaches & Water Sports: Swimming, surfing, and kayaking are major draws, particularly in Cape Hatteras.
    • Historic Sites:
      Visit the Wright Brothers National Memorial in Kill Devil Hills, Roanoke Island (site of the Lost Colony), and various lighthouses.
    • Outdoor Activities: Explore Jockey’s Ridge State Park (massive natural sand dunes) and view wild horses in Corolla.
    • Local Dining: Enjoy fresh, local seafood in towns like Nags Head, Duck, and Kitty Hawk. 
    When to Visit & Tips 
    • Summer (June–August): Peak season with high temperatures (mid-80s°F) and fully active, busy attractions.
    • Spring/Fall: Ideal for lower prices and fewer crowds.
    • Accommodation: The area is known for large vacation rental homes rather than hotels.
    • Safety Notice: Visitors should be aware of coastal erosion, particularly in areas like Buxton and Rodanthe, where beach closures can occur due to unsafe, collapsing homes. 
    What the OBX is Known For 
    • Barrier Islands: A unique, fragile chain of islands separated from the mainland.
    • "Graveyard of the Atlantic": Famous for many shipwrecks, with museums dedicated to maritime history.
    • Outdoor Adventure: A hub for fishing, kiteboarding, and hang gliding.
    • TV Series: Outer Banks, the Netflix drama series, has brought new attention to the area, with a fifth and final season scheduled to premiere in 2026. 
    Nearby Attractions 
    • Roanoke Island: Home to the Elizabethan Gardens and the Lost Colony outdoor drama.
    • Currituck Mainland: Offers mainland activities and wildlife viewing.
    • Cedar Island/Ocracoke: Accessible by ferry, providing a more remote, scenic experience. 
    Note: For the latest information on events and seasonal activities, visit OuterBanks.org.
